doc.title: Hank Cicalo interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 30, 2022

title: Getting the Monkees to play: Micky's drum setup
summary: Hank says Chip Douglas came later, and tells how Micky learned drums on a set arranged backwards at home.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: What possessed you to try to get the members of the Monkees to play their own instruments?
I didn’t really have much to do with that. Let’s see —

Well Chip came in later. I had already done two albums, but that was all right. When Chip came in they all wanted to do their own stuff and their own playing, so it was a little strange. A lot of them were not players before they began. For example in the drums

Mickey didn’t, he never played drums before. But they wanted to make him the drummer. So Columbia sends the drums over to his house and where the guys dropped the drums is where he learned to play. So the snare was on the wrong side and the toms were on the wrong side. But that’s the way they set it up and it was three or four weeks every day, every night, he played those drums. When he came to the studio I set up the drums the way I normally would. And he looked at them and he said, “No, I don’t know what to do with this.” Because for weeks now he’s been playing all by himself at his house bashing away and the snare wasn’t in the right place for him in the studio, it was on the wrong side. It should have been on the right side, it’s on the left side. That kind of thing. And I had to adjust that. Does that make sense?
It does. It’s like learning a guitar left handed or backwards.
Right. Exactly. Exactly. And a lot of those things they didn’t play very well.
